correctness.rationale: The chain 0<1<2 is forced by torsion H1; its Euler characteristic gives total arrows ab+2. The sink-graph long exact sequence forces connectedness because H1 is finite, and shows H1 generated by a-1; applying the same argument to the opposite category gives b-1 generators. The H1 of a wedge of r projective planes requires r generators, so \(a,b\ge r+1\). The explicit (r+1)x(r+1) composition table has \(c=r^2+1\) arrows; its incidence graph is r four-cycles sharing a single edge plus leaves and its map to the base wedge of circles winds twice in each independent factor. Thus its classifying space is the desired wedge. Exact integer Smith tests agree for \(r=1\)..5; finite tests are not the infinite proof.

It gives a sharp quadratic price for holding the number of categorical objects at its known minimum, directly motivated by the object-versus-parallel-morphism trade-off in the primary paper, and distinguishes torsion first homology from previous sphere-wedge optimizations.
